paragraphs: Mali was not on any European map before this trip. The Catalan Atlas, drawn on Majorca fifty years later in 1375, put it there: a crowned Mansa Musa sits south of the Sahara holding a gold nugget, with a caption naming him the richest king in the region because of the gold mined in his territory.

Al-Umari, a Cairo official who gathered accounts of the visit about a decade later, wrote that Mansa Musa gave away so much gold in alms and trade that the metal did not regain its value in the city for years; later estimates of the slump range from about ten to twelve years. Chroniclers also say he tried to undo the damage on the way home by borrowing gold back from Cairo's merchants at interest, though how much he recovered is not recorded.
